title:
Though it’s conventional to think of dals as always being finished with a tadka of something or the other—seeds or onions or garlic or chillies or all of the above fried in hot ghee/oil—some of my favourite ways of making mushoor/masoor and moog/moong dal are actually without tadka. You can find these recipes on my blog (link in profile). 

This recipe tonight is a variation on my favourite no tadka/everything cooked together mushoor/masoor dal. The variation comes from one of my aunts who also adds the panch phoron that would normally go in the tadka in with everything else. Then you pressure cook it and add dhania patta/cilantro at the end. This is very much a convenience recipe but it’s no less delicious for that.

Rough recipe for what you see: 1 cup masoor dal, rinsed + 4.5 cups water + 1 medium red onion, sliced + 10-12 cloves of garlic, whole + 3/4 tspn haldi + 1 tspn panch phoron + 1/2 cup chopped tomato + 3 whole Thai chillies + 1 tblspn ghee + salt. Give it a stir and cook under pressure for two whistles in your old-school whistling pressure cooker. Let the pressure subside (or cool it quickly under running water in the sink), open, stir well, add the dhania and stir again. Eat with rice with a big squeeze of lime and achaar on the side (or just out of a bowl). Be happy.

Don’t have an old-school pressure cooker? Bring everything to a boil on the stovetop, stir the dal down and cook covered at a simmer for 20-30 minutes. Have an InstantPot or some other new-fangled pressure cooker? You’re on your own.

It’s not considered very Bengali, by the way, to put tomato in dal. But whatever. Also, if you want to make this #vegan, substitute a neutral oil for the ghee. Want the dal to be thinner? Add an extra 1/2 cup of water.
 
Also by the way: the song playing in the Reel, De Bhi Chuke Hum, from the film Jaal (1952) is one of very few duets between Kishore Kumar and Geeta Dutt.
